payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet

condition.question: To what extent does the edited image place a frog inside the toilet bowl, as requested?
condition.criteria: Compare SOURCE and EDITED. Assess the requested change as a whole: a frog must be visibly positioned within the toilet bowl, not merely on the lid or floor. Compare the bowl contents in SOURCE and EDITED so a pre-existing object is not mistaken for the requested frog. A frog newly visible within the bowl is concrete progress; frogs elsewhere do not count as bowl placement and do not negate a frog that is in the bowl. Score full only when the requested bowl placement is clearly achieved; score partial when there is concrete but incomplete bowl placement.
condition.binding: SOURCE: the toilet and its bowl contents in the input image, including the small dark object already visible in the bowl. EDITED: the same toilet; distinguish the open bowl from the raised lid and surrounding floor, and compare bowl contents with SOURCE to identify any frog visibly placed within the bowl.
condition.source_quote: Put a frog in the toilet
condition.aspect: A frog is placed inside the toilet bowl.
condition.endpoint: A frog is visibly inside the toilet bowl.
condition.necessity: The requested edit is to put a frog in the toilet; placing a frog inside the bowl directly fulfills that request, while source/edit comparison prevents counting a pre-existing bowl object as the edit.
condition.zero_when: No frog has been added or placed inside the toilet bowl; a pre-existing bowl object or frogs only on the lid or floor do not count.
condition.half_when: There is concrete but incomplete evidence of a frog being placed in the bowl—for example, a frog is only partly positioned within the bowl or its placement is substantially ambiguous—while a substantial part of the requested bowl placement remains unfulfilled. A clearly placed frog in the bowl is not made partial merely by additional frogs elsewhere.
condition.full_when: At least one frog absent from the source is clearly and substantially positioned within the toilet bowl, rather than only on the lid or floor, so the requested placement is achieved. Additional frogs elsewhere do not negate this placement.
